# SOP-P3-L3-03 First-article inspection - Machining line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-016, MM-P3-L3-HP03, MM-P3-L3-SB01

Purpose
1. Define the controlled first-article inspection (FAI) workflow for parts produced on P3-L3 machining line. This procedure ensures the first part off a run meets drawing and process requirements before full production release.

Background and scope
2. This SOP applies to first articles produced on EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03. It covers visual, dimensional, functional, and process-verification checks, equipment pre-checks, acceptance criteria review, and records retention. For maintenance-related tasks refer to MM-P3-L3-HP03 and MM-P3-L3-SB01. For engineering changes consult ECN-2026-016.

Preconditions
3. The work order and applicable release documentation must be available at the workstation. The machine program and fixture setup must be loaded as released in the manufacturing system. The part drawing and inspection criteria must be referenced and verified against the latest release. The operator must have completed line-specific setup training and hold current qualifications.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Required PPE: safety glasses, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, safety shoes, and any task-specific respiratory protection indicated by the plant safety officer. Ensure PPE is donned before entering the machining and shot blast areas.

Critical material and equipment references
5. Verify the lubricant and wear items for the shot blast cabinet prior to running the first article:
- The lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709.
- The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is 105 N·m.
6. Confirm tooling and gages are calibrated and their status is current in the calibration system. Use gage blocks and reference standards traceable to the calibration lab.

Step-by-step procedure
7. Step 1 — Pre-run verification
7.1 Confirm work order and part revision. Verify fixture orientation and clamping points. Check tool offsets and program match released operation. Validate coolant and chip management are functional.

8. Step 2 — Machine warm-up and dry run
8.1 Perform a dry run with fixture empty to verify program motion and collision clearance. Observe for abnormal sounds or interference. Correct any program or setup issues before inserting raw material.

9. Step 3 — First-article setup
9.1 Mount raw material and perform single-cycle machining to produce the first article. Record the program ID and operator initials in the run log.

10. Step 4 — Primary inspection at machine (operator)
10.1 Perform visual inspection for surface condition, burrs, and secure fastenings. Verify critical features with at-machine gages as specified on the drawing. Flag any deviations immediately and notify process control.

11. Step 5 — Shot blast and surface preparation
11.1 After primary inspection, move the first article to EQ-P3-L3-SB01 for shot blasting per the surface finish requirement. Verify that consumables and the lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is present and correct prior to operation.
11.2 Reinspect blasted surface for profile, cleanliness, and finish consistency.

12. Step 6 — Secondary inspection (QC)
12.1 QC performs full dimensional inspection using calibrated instruments. Record actual measurements against drawing tolerances on the First-Article Inspection Report (FAIR).
12.2 Functional checks include assembly fit with mating components and verification of critical form features. Document any out-of-tolerance dimensions with disposition recommendation.

13. Step 7 — Process verification and hold point
13.1 If the FAIR passes, QC signs the report and releases the lot for production. If any nonconformance is found, initiate containment and hold subsequent production until corrective action and revalidation are complete. Reference ECN-2026-016 for any engineering changes required.

14. Step 8 — Example nonconformance workflow
14.1 Example: If a critical bore diameter is out of tolerance, QC annotates the FAIR, tags the part as HOLD, notifies Engineering and Maintenance, and stops the run. Engineering evaluates if program correction or fixture adjustment is required. Maintenance performs mechanical checks per MM-P3-L3-HP03 or MM-P3-L3-SB01 as applicable.

Records to keep
15. Maintain the following records in the document control system:
- First-Article Inspection Report (FAIR) with dimensional data and signatures.  
- Machine program ID and revision log.  
- Tooling and gage calibration certificates or references.  
- Process setup photos showing tool orientation and fixture placement.  
- Any nonconformance reports and associated dispositions.  
Store FAIR and associated records per plant retention policy.

Rationale and acceptance criteria
16. The two-stage inspection (operator primary and QC secondary) reduces risk of latent defects entering bulk production. Operator checks catch gross issues; QC confirms dimensional and functional compliance. Acceptance requires all critical dimensions within tolerance and no functional failures. Any deviation must be resolved via formal ECN process when redesign or program change is necessary.

Responsibilities
17. Operators: execute setup, perform primary inspection, and document program and tooling used.  
QC: perform full FAIR, evaluate results, and authorize production release.  
Engineering: support disposition and corrective action for failed FAIs and issue ECN-2026-016 if design or program changes are required.  
Maintenance: perform mechanical checks and corrective maintenance per MM-P3-L3-HP03 and MM-P3-L3-SB01.

Sign-off
18. Completed FAIR must be signed by:
- Operator (printed name and signature)  
- QC inspector (printed name and signature)  
- Production supervisor (printed name and signature)  
- Engineering representative (printed name and signature) if any nonconformance required disposition

Appendix
19. Examples of FAIR entries, gage checklists, and photo documentation templates are available in the document control folder associated with this SOP. Refer to ECN-2026-016 for change history and to MM-P3-L3-HP03 and MM-P3-L3-SB01 for maintenance procedures related to the equipment listed in this SOP.
